full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 21.05.2015, passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 32 of 2001, allowing the appeal upon setting aside those of the trial court dated 26.10.2000, passed in Title Suit No. 105 of 1998, dismissing the suit. 

 5. The trial court dismissed the suit, on contest, by judgment and decree dated 26.10.2000 against which the plaintiffs prefetred First Appeal No. 32 of 2001 before the High Court Division and a Division Bench of the said Division allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court by judgment and decree dated 21.05.2015. Being aggrieved, the defendants preferred this civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 6. Mr. M Quamrul Hoque Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that Exhibits-'Ka' and 'Kha' make it clear that the defendant-appellants have already adjusted all the loans facilitated/provided by the plaintiff-respondent Bank; on the contrary, the plaintiff-respondent bank failed to pro-duce any authentic document to show that any of such facilitated loans remained an-ear or unpaid. PM-1 in His examination-in-chief and on recall produced certain documents, to which the defendant-petitioners raised vehement objection on the ground that in the plaint nothing has been mentioned regarding the said documents. In spite of such vigorous objection, the trial court took those documents into consideration and marked those as Exhibit Nos. 7, 8, 8(ka) to 8 (ha) and 16 series to 32. The said documents do not corroborate oral evidence of PW-1. He failed to give any satisfactory answer, in his cross examination, as to the authenticity of those documents. He next submits that a large amount of stock-lots of the defendant-petitioners were stolen from the custody of the plaintiff-respondent bank, but in spite of repeated requests from the petitioners, the plaintiff did not take any step to recover the same resulting huge loss to defendant-petitioners' company. He further submits that, the High Court Division failed to appreciate that at the time of mortgaging the schedule property, the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 were minors, but no permission were taken from the court; hence such act cannot impose liability upon them. The High Court Division with-out considering all these factual aspects and material evidence allowed the appeal upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. As such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in the eye of law. 

 7. Mr. Ahsanul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of plaintiff-respondent No.1, Bank, made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division and prayed for dismissal of the present petition. 

 12. The defendant-petitioner No.1 company is denying all the above mentioned liabilities on the plea that the signatures of those documents were obtained by the bank in blank papers from the Managing Director of the defendant-petitioner-company and falsely created those abovementioned documents. But fact remains, the defendant company failed to prove such plea by producing proper evidence either oral or documentary. On the contrary, on perusal of Exhibit-5 it appears that on 22.07.1993 the Managing Director of the defendant-petitioner No.1 applied to the plaintiff-respondent bank describing the necessity for carrying out BMRE and he needs further loan facility to make the company a profitable one. On the basis of such application the bank granted another amount of Tk. 2.40 crore as loan on 13.10.1993. Such application proves that the petitioner-company had more transactions with plaintiff-respondent bank beyond the two admitted loans. Moreover, the defendant-petitioner company admit-ted that on 08.06.1999 a large number of stock was stolen from the godown of the company which was under the custody of the plaintiff-bank. So, if the defendant company did not have any transaction with the plaintiff-bank then there would have been no question of keeping goods, in the godown under the custody of the bank. Unfortunately the Adalat without considering all the above mentioned evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit which is not sustainable in the eye of law. Consequently, in the first appeal the High Court Division rightly set aside such finding and decision of the Adalat and decreed the suit.
